items.text: The broad nineteenth-century Italian unification movement combining nationalist ideology, diplomacy, war and popular action.
Garibaldi’s conquest of Sicily and Naples, handed to Victor Emmanuel II for monarchist unification.

Prepare the four actors (Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II) and show explicitly how unification required ideas, diplomacy, war and popular action together; draw the sequence of territorial additions (1859, 1860, 1861, 1866, 1870).
Practise one analytical outline answering: “How did Mazzini, Cavour, Garibaldi and Victor Emmanuel II each contribute differently to Italian unification?”
Do not say unification was completed in 1861; Venetia (1866) and Rome (1870) came later.
Do not present Mazzini, Cavour and Garibaldi as political allies with identical goals; they differed substantially in method and ultimate aim.
Do not ignore foreign powers; France, Austria and Prussia were crucial to the timing of unification.
Giuseppe Mazzini promoted republican nationalism and founded Young Italy in 1831.
Count Cavour used modernisation and diplomacy to challenge Austria; war in 1859 helped Piedmont gain Lombardy.
Garibaldi’s 1860 campaign brought the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies into the unification process.
The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861; Venetia was added in 1866 and Rome in 1870.
Explain unification as the combination of nationalist ideas, Piedmontese state power, foreign diplomacy, and Garibaldi’s popular military action — never as one figure’s achievement alone.
Keep the territorial timeline precise: 1859 (Lombardy), 1860 (Sicily/Naples), 1861 (Kingdom proclaimed), 1866 (Venetia), 1870 (Rome).
